title: Artisan Command
description: An Artisan command. A first-class Document, like a Menu: it runs a chain of actions and can take typed arguments. The resolved arguments reach the menus it opens as placeholders.

schema.description: Schema version. Fixed, so that migrations can apply on load.

id.description: LEGACY, ignored. A Document's identity is its file name (the reader overrides this value and reports a mismatch). Still read in older Projects; never written.

name.description: The command name as typed in game, without the slash. Optional: defaults to the file name (written only when it differs). Lowercase letters, digits, _ and -. Unique on the server.

aliases.description: Other names for the same command.

permission.description: Permission required to run the command. Absent: anyone can run it (subject to requirements).

description.description: Short description shown in the server's command list, visible to players. One string (every language) or a `{language: text}` map.

enabled.description: false: the command is not registered (nothing is deleted) and its name stays free.

notes.description: The admin's internal notes, never shown to players. Unlike YAML comments, they survive the editor.

arguments.description: Positional arguments, in order. Required arguments come before optional ones.

requirements.description: Conditions checked before running, all required. If one fails, `fallback` (if any) runs instead of the actions.

actions.description: The action chain run when the command is called: a list of steps (or a single step). A plain string is the legacy Action DSL. Resolved arguments are available as %args_<name>% and {arg}.

steps.description: Legacy form of `actions`: still read, never written.

fallback.description: Actions run when the requirements fail, typically a send_message saying why.

cooldown.description: Cooldown between runs. Per player by default.

metadata.description: Metadata computed by the editor. Not edited by hand.

subcommands.description: Subcommands, typed after the name and before the arguments (`/ah sell 100`). Any depth.

Cooldown.description: Cooldown between runs, per player (default) or server-wide.

id.description: Cooldown id, shared by the runs of the same scope.

message.description: Message shown while the cooldown runs: an {i18n:key} reference or MiniMessage text.

Argument.description: A typed positional argument. Its resolved value is the placeholder %args_<name>% (with sub-fields for complex types).

name.description: Argument name, exposed as the placeholder %args_<name>%.

type.description: Argument type; sets parsing and tab completion. player: online or offline (resolved by UUID). online_player: must be online. enum: values fixed by the admin (see `values`).

required.description: false: the argument may be left out. Optional arguments come after required ones.

default.description: Value used when the argument is left out. For a `player` argument, the reserved value `"{sender}"` means whoever typed the command: `/cmd [player]` targets yourself unless you name someone. From the console there is no sender player, so the argument stays absent.

values.description: Allowed values of an enum argument, also used for tab completion. Required when type is "enum".

description.description: Description shown in the help and on hover in the editor.

LocalizedText.description: One text for every language, or a language → text map (fallback: the default language, then the first one present).

Subcommand.description: A `subcommands` node, reached by its name or an alias after its parent's. Without `actions`, it shows the usage of the subcommands the player may run.

name.description: The word typed after the parent's.

aliases.description: Other names for the same command.

permission.description: Checked on top of the parents' permissions: a subcommand never widens access.

enabled.description: false: the subcommand does not exist; its name falls through to the parent's arguments.

notes.description: The admin's internal notes, never shown to players. Unlike YAML comments, they survive the editor.

arguments.description: Positional arguments, in order. Required arguments come before optional ones.

requirements.description: Conditions checked before running, all required. If one fails, `fallback` (if any) runs instead of the actions.

actions.description: The action chain run when the command is called: a list of steps (or a single step). A plain string is the legacy Action DSL. Resolved arguments are available as %args_<name>% and {arg}.

fallback.description: Actions run when the requirements fail, typically a send_message saying why.

cooldown.description: This node's own cooldown. Without `id`, the id is the command path (`ah sell`).
